key_insight: X-AgentRed shows that personal AI agents can fail in surprising ways when they chain benign actions across multiple services, so red-teaming must explore real cross-service paths instead of relying only on prompt-based guesses. The paper’s core insight is that compositional harm emerges from interactions, not just from any single tool or action.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of proactively finding unintended or harmful outcomes in personal agents that operate across evolving multi-service ecosystems, where actions in one service can trigger cascading effects in others.
method: Systematically explores cross-service action paths rather than only asking an LLM to imagine harmful scenarios.
Red-teams personal agents in multi-service environments to uncover compositional failures that arise from accumulated side effects.
Targets evolving ecosystems, helping identify vulnerabilities that simple task/environment descriptions often miss.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights a more realistic and scalable way to safety-test tool-using agents before deployment. It helps reduce hidden failure modes in assistants that interact with multiple apps, services, and APIs.
visual_elements: Flow diagram showing a user request branching through multiple services and ending in an unintended outcome
Before/after comparison of prompt-only red-teaming vs. path-based red-teaming
Network graph of services and tool calls with highlighted harmful interaction chains
Icon set for agents, tools, services, and cascading risk
paper_title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
paper_authors: Yeonsung Jung, Zhiyuan Wang, Zifan Wang, Vítor Albiero, Benjamin Newman
